entities.summary:
Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus Maximus was a consul of the Roman Republic in 283 BC.

As a key figure during the late Hellenistic period, Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus Maximus played a significant role in shaping the course of Roman history. He was part of the Roman aristocracy and held considerable influence in the governance of Rome.

Calvinus Maximus's tenure as consul coincided with the rise of the Seleucid Empire under Antiochus III, who would eventually clash with Rome in the First Macedonian War. This conflict had far-reaching consequences for the Mediterranean world, including the redrawing of borders and the establishment of new trade routes.

Despite his limited time in office, Calvinus Maximus left a lasting legacy as a symbol of Roman power and prestige. His name became synonymous with the ideals of civic duty and leadership that defined the Roman Republic.

The sheer magnitude of this event can be distilled into a single, striking quote: 'Virtus et fortitudo vincunt omnia' ('Virtue and strength conquer all'). This phrase, attributed to Calvinus Maximus himself, encapsulates the essence of his enduring impact on Western civilization.
